title: Guide for authors
text:
Include extra metadata in the front matter section of a notebook. Possible values include:

authors
abstract
keywords

For example, to list the notebook’s authors add their details to the first cell of the notebook like this.
---
authors:
    - name: Tim Sherratt
      orcid: http://orcid.org/0000-0001-7956-4498
      url: https://timsherratt.au
---
Front matter rules: - has to be in the first cell of the notebook - cell has to be set to ‘Markdown’ - data has to be valid YAML - YAML data has to be enclosed top and bottom by --- lines

title: Guide for authors
text:
Labelling cells and content
By labelling code and Markdown cells they can used in cross-references or embedded elsewhere in the book.
Note that labels are accessible across the whole site, not just a notebook, so should be unique. Quarto defines a set of prefixes that should be used in labels, eg: ‘fig’, ‘tbl’, and ‘sec’ for figures, tables and sections.
To label a section, add {#sec-my-section-name} after a heading. For example:
## Cool things about Hansard {#sec-my-cool-hansard-things}
To label an image add {#fig-my-image} after the standard Markdown image embed link:
![](parliament-house.jpeg) {#fig-parliament-house}
To label an image with a caption:
::: {#fig-parliament-house}

![](parliament-house.jpeg)

Parliament House in Canberra
:::
To label a code cell that produces a chart add #| label: fig-my-chart and #| fig-caption: My interesting chart to the very top of the cell:
#| label: fig-sitting-days
#| fig-cap: Number of sitting days per year for the House of Representatives and the Senate

# Code goes here

title: Guide for authors
text:
Links and cross-references
To create an internal link to another notebook, use standard Markdown syntax with the full or relative path to the notebook in the file structure, including the file extension.
For example, [introduction to Hansard](/hansard/hansard-intro) produces:

Here’s an introduction to Hansard

To create an internal link to a heading in another notebook, use standard Markdown syntax with the full path to the notebook and the heading’s HTML id. For example to link to the ‘Quarto’ heading in the ‘contributing’ notebook, use [](/contributing/contributing#quarto):

This site uses quarto.

You can also use the @fig-sitting-days shorthand:
Figure 1 shows the number of sitting days for each house of parliament.

title: Parliamentary Handbook API
text:
The Parliamentary Handbook includes a simple API that you can use to get the data about parliament and parliamentarians in machine-readable form.
Aggregated data about individuals can be accessed via: https://handbookapi.aph.gov.au/api/individuals/. However, this data only includes a summary of the available information for each person. There are a variety of other endpoints that can be used to access the full data. For example:

title: Parliamentarians
text:
What do we know about the people whose words are recorded in Hansard? The Parliamentary Handbook provides a wealth of information on the make up of the Australian Parliament, including biographical details of all parliamentarians from 1901. The Parliamentary Handbook includes a simple API that you can use to get the data about parliamentarians in machine-readable form.
Here we’ll use this data to provide some snapshots of members of the Australian Parliament.
Now we have the data we can slice it in different ways to gain some understanding of the make up of parliament.

title: Parliamentarians
text:
Gender
The data from the Parliamentary Handbook includes a field for Gender. We can aggregate data from this field to generate some overviews.


Code
gender_total = df["Gender"].value_counts().to_frame().reset_index()
gender_house = df.loc[df["ElectedMemberNo"] > -1]["Gender"].value_counts().to_frame().reset_index()
gender_senate = df.loc[df["ElectedSenatorNo"] > -1]["Gender"].value_counts().to_frame().reset_index()

# Create the base chart
gender_base = alt.Chart().encode(
    theta=alt.Theta("count").stack(True),
    color=alt.Color("Gender").legend(None),
    tooltip=[alt.Tooltip("count", title="number of parliamentarians"), alt.Tooltip("Gender", title="gender")]
).properties(width="container")

# Both houses
total_base = gender_base.properties(data=gender_total)
# Create the pie segments
total_pie = total_base.mark_arc()
# Create the text labels
total_text = total_base.mark_text(radius=170, size=12).encode(text="Gender:N")
# Combine pie and labels
chart_total = alt.layer(total_pie, total_text, padding=20)

# House of Reps
house_base = gender_base.properties(data=gender_house)
house_pie = house_base.mark_arc(outerRadius=120)
house_text = house_base.mark_text(radius=140, size=12).encode(text="Gender:N")
chart_house = alt.layer(house_pie, house_text, padding=20)

# Senate
senate_base = gender_base.properties(data=gender_senate)
senate_pie = senate_base.mark_arc(outerRadius=120)
senate_text = senate_base.mark_text(radius=140, size=12).encode(text="Gender:N")
chart_senate = alt.layer(senate_pie, senate_text, padding=20)

# Need to display all charts together like this for Quarto to lay them out
display(chart_total, chart_house, chart_senate)

(b) House of Representatives














(c) Senate







Figure 1: Number of parliamentarians by gender (1901 – present)




Every federal election results in a new ‘parliament’, and each parliament is given a consecutive number. So the very first parliamant was number 1. The parliamentarians data includes a list of the parliaments that each member was a part of. We can use this to explore how the gender composition of the parliament has changed over time.


Code
# Explode to create a row for each parliament
df_parls = df.explode("RepresentedParliaments", ignore_index=True)

parl_gender_base = alt.Chart().mark_bar().encode(
    x=alt.X("parls:O").title("parliament number"),
    y=alt.Y("count:Q").title("number of members").stack(True),
    color="Gender",
    tooltip=[alt.Tooltip("parls", title="parliament"), alt.Tooltip("Gender", title="gender"), alt.Tooltip("count", title="number of members")]
).properties(width="container")

parl_gender = df_parls.value_counts(["Gender", "RepresentedParliaments"]).to_frame().reset_index()
parl_gender.columns = ["Gender", "parls", "count"]
parl_gender_chart = parl_gender_base.properties(data=parl_gender)

display(parl_gender_chart)










Figure 2: Gender breakdown by parliament (both houses combined)




The aggregated data from the Parliamentary Handbook doesn’t specify which house a member was in during a particular parliament. To find that, we can compare their service details with the dates of each parliament. Once we’ve split the parliaments data into houses, we can chart the gender breakdown by house.


Code
df_parl_dates = pd.read_json("https://handbookapi.aph.gov.au/api/StatisticalInformation/Parliaments", convert_dates=["DateElection", "DateDissolution"])

def is_in_range(dates, parl_num):
    date_start, date_end = list(df_parl_dates.iloc[df_parl_dates["Number"] == parl_num][["DateElection", "DateDissolution"]].values[0])
    test_dates = [datetime.fromisoformat(d) for d in dates]
    if pd.notnull(date_end):
        return date_start <= test_dates[1] and date_end >= test_dates[0]
    else:
        return date_start <= test_dates[1] and datetime.now() >= test_dates[0]

def check_dates(dates, parls):
    checked_parls = []
    for parl_num in parls:
        for date in dates:
            if is_in_range(date, parl_num):
                checked_parls.append(parl_num)
    return list(set(checked_parls))

def find_house_parliaments(row):
    if len(row["MPorSenator"]) == 1:
        if row["MPorSenator"][0] == "Member":
            house_parls = row["RepresentedParliaments"]
            senate_parls = []
        else:
            senate_parls = row["RepresentedParliaments"]
            house_parls = []
    else:
        senate_dates = []
        house_dates = []
        services = row["PartyParliamentaryService"]
        electorates = row["ElectorateService"]
        elec_dates = [e["ServiceStart"] for e in electorates]
        for service in services:
            if service["DateStart"] in elec_dates:
                house_dates.append([service["DateStart"], service["DateEnd"]])
            else:
                senate_dates.append([service["DateStart"], service["DateEnd"]])
        house_parls = check_dates(house_dates, row["RepresentedParliaments"])
        senate_parls = check_dates(senate_dates, row["RepresentedParliaments"])
        
    return pd.Series([house_parls, senate_parls])

df[["house_parls", "senate_parls"]] = df.apply(find_house_parliaments, axis=1)

df_house_parls = df.explode("house_parls", ignore_index=True)
df_senate_parls = df.explode("senate_parls", ignore_index=True)

parl_gender_house = df_house_parls.value_counts(["Gender", "house_parls"]).to_frame().reset_index()
parl_gender_house.columns = ["Gender", "parls", "count"]
parl_gender_house_chart = parl_gender_base.properties(data=parl_gender_house, height=200)

parl_gender_senate = df_senate_parls.value_counts(["Gender", "senate_parls"]).to_frame().reset_index()
parl_gender_senate.columns = ["Gender", "parls", "count"]
parl_gender_senate_chart = parl_gender_base.properties(data=parl_gender_senate, height=200)
parl_gender_senate_chart.encoding.y = parl_gender_senate_chart.encoding.y.scale(domain=(0, 160))

display(parl_gender_house_chart, parl_gender_senate_chart)















(a) House of Representatives
















(b) Senate







Figure 3: Gender breakdown by parliament and house

title: Parliamentarians
text:
Age
What is the average age of each parliament?


Code
def get_opening_date(sessions):
    starting_dates = []
    for session in sessions:
        starting_dates.append(session["DateOpening"])
    return pd.to_datetime(sorted(starting_dates)[0])
    
df_parl_dates["opening"] = df_parl_dates["Sessions"].apply(get_opening_date)
df_parl_openings = df_parl_dates[["Number", "opening"]]

def calculate_age(row):
    opening = row["opening"]
    born = row["DateOfBirth"]
    return opening.year - born.year - ((opening.month, opening.day) < (born.month, born.day))

df_parls_ages = pd.merge(df_parls, df_parl_openings, how="left", left_on="RepresentedParliaments", right_on="Number")
df_parls_ages["DateOfBirth"] = pd.to_datetime(df_parls_ages["DateOfBirth"], format='ISO8601')
df_parls_ages["age"] = df_parls_ages.apply(calculate_age, axis=1)

parl_ages = df_parls_ages.groupby(["Number", "opening"])["age"].agg(["mean", "min", "max"]).reset_index()

age_base = alt.Chart(parl_ages).encode(
    x=alt.X("Number:O").title("parliament number"),
).properties(width="container")

mean_ages = age_base.mark_line(point=True).encode(
    y=alt.Y("mean:Q").scale(domain=(40, 60)).title("mean age of members"),
    tooltip=[alt.Tooltip("Number", title="parliament"), alt.Tooltip("opening", title="opening date"), alt.Tooltip("mean", title="mean of ages"), "max", "min"]
).properties(width="container")

age_intervals = age_base.mark_area(opacity=0.2).encode(
    alt.Y("max:Q").scale(domain=(20, 90)),
    alt.Y2("min:Q"),
    tooltip=[alt.Tooltip("Number", title="parliament"), alt.Tooltip("opening", title="opening date"), alt.Tooltip("mean", title="mean of ages"), "max", "min"]
).properties(width="container")

display(mean_ages, age_intervals + mean_ages)













(a) Mean age of members at the start of each parliament












(b)

title: About this site
text: This site was created by the Reusable and Accessible Public Interest Documents (RAPID-CDL) project, part of ARDC’s Community Data Lab. The RAPID-CDL project aims to make public interest documents such as parliamentary proceedings, inquiry submissions, hearing transcripts, and ministerial records more accessible and usable for researchers across Australia.

title: An example notebook
text:
The cell below generates a chart. Note that the cell has been labelled using #| label: sitting-days-chart this means the cell can be referenced elsewhere using sitting-days-chart.
If you look in the cell metadata you’ll see it includes the remove-cell tag. This means the cell and its output won’t be included in the final book. Instead we’ll embed the chart in a figure below so we can add a caption and it will be automatically numbered.

import pandas as pd
import altair as alt

df = pd.read_json("https://handbookapi.aph.gov.au/api/StatisticalInformation/SittingDaysPerYear")

dfs = []
for house in ["Reps", "Senate"]:
    df_h = df[["Year", f"{house}Days"]]
    df_h["house"] = house
    df_h.columns = ["year", "days", "house"]
    dfs.append(df_h)
df_split = pd.concat(dfs)

ticks = [t for t in range(1900, 2030, 5)]
alt.Chart(df_split).mark_bar().encode(
    x=alt.X("year:O").axis(values=ticks).title(None),
    y=alt.Y("days:Q").title(None),
    row=alt.Row("house").title("number of days"),
    color=alt.Color("house").legend(None),
    tooltip=["year:O", "house:N", "days:Q"]
).properties(height=200, width=600, padding=20)
